This is a formal internal appeal of the denial shown on the Empire Harbor Health Explanation of Benefits dated September 2, 2026, for laboratory services provided on August 11, 2026. The stated reason is a claim submission or billing error and a missing or invalid diagnosis code. I ask the plan to overturn this denial and pay the claim. This appeal is filed within the 180-day window allowed for internal appeals [[cite:fed.internal_appeal.filing_window]].

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text:
On August 11, 2026, I received a comprehensive metabolic panel (CPT 80053) and a lipid panel (CPT 80061) from MetroLab Diagnostics, an in-network provider. The tests were ordered by [ADD: name of the ordering provider].

The amount billed was $244. The plan paid $0 and listed $244 as my responsibility.

The denial reason is quoted here word for word from the Explanation of Benefits: "CO-16: Claim/service lacks information or has submission/billing error(s) which is needed for adjudication. M-76: Missing/incomplete/invalid diagnosis or condition."

sections.heading: Why the denial should be overturned
sections.text:
This denial does not rest on coverage. The plan has not found that the laboratory tests were unnecessary, excluded, or outside my benefits. The denial rests entirely on a claim-form problem: a missing or invalid diagnosis code on the submission from MetroLab Diagnostics.

The services were performed and were ordered by my treating provider for [ADD: the reason the tests were ordered, such as monitoring a condition]. A supporting statement and the order with the diagnosis are available from [ADD: name of the ordering provider].

I have asked MetroLab Diagnostics to submit a corrected claim with the complete diagnosis information. [ADD: date you contacted the provider, and the date they said the corrected claim would be sent].

Because the provider is in network, the billing paperwork is the provider's responsibility, not mine. A coding omission on the provider's claim form should not shift $244 to me while the correction is being made.

The denial notice must state the specific reason, the plan provision relied on, and exactly what added information is needed and why [[cite:fed.notice.required_content]]. I am also entitled, on request, to be told the diagnosis and treatment codes used for this claim and what each one means [[cite:fed.claim_file.codes_meaning]].

sections.heading: What I am asking for
sections.text:
1. A complete copy of the claim file and every document, record, rule, guideline, or protocol relied on for this claim, free of charge [[cite:fed.claim_file.free_copies]].

2. The specific plan provision or claims-processing rule applied, and the name and credentials of the person who reviewed the claim [[cite:fed.claim_file.free_copies]].

3. A written decision on this appeal within the required time frame for care already received [[cite:fed.internal_appeal.decision_windows]].

4. The diagnosis code and treatment codes the plan received on this claim, and what each code means, so the correction can be confirmed [[cite:fed.claim_file.codes_meaning]].

5. Reprocessing and payment of the claim as soon as the corrected claim from MetroLab Diagnostics is received, with no balance held against me in the meantime.

I can be reached at [ADD: your phone number] or [ADD: your email address]. Please send all correspondence to the address above.

If the plan does not fully overturn this denial, I reserve the right to pursue an external appeal in New York within the applicable time frames [[cite:ny.external_appeal.scope]] [[cite:ny.external_appeal.decision_windows]]. I also reserve the right to proceed if the plan does not follow the required claims procedure [[cite:fed.deemed_exhaustion]].

Sincerely,

[ADD: your full name]
Member ID: EHH-3320917
